overall_design: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) on CD45+ immune cells isolated from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), tumor tissues (T), and peritumor tissues (PT) of HBV-HCC (PBMC: n=4; T: n=3; PT: n=3) and MASH-HCC (PBMC: n=4; T: n=2; PT: n=2) patients. Integrative bioinformatics analyses were conducted to characterize T cell subsets, their functional states, and intercellular crosstalk. Validation induced multiplex immunohistochemistry and Flow cytometry on patients.
summary: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) exhibits remarkable etiological heterogeneity, with hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) emerging as two leading causes. The tumor microenvironment (TME), particularly T cell subsets, plays a pivotal role in tumor progression and immunotherapy response. However, the etiology-specific T cell landscapes in HBV-HCC and MASH-HCC remain poorly characterized.

type: Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing
